summary: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires everyone else to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy — often with long interview wait times.

primarySources.name: ESTA — Official U.S. Customs and Border Protection application site
U.S. Department of State — U.S. Visas
U.S. Customs and Border Protection — International Visitors

defaultSource.name: eCFR — 8 CFR 212.1, Documentary requirements for nonimmigrants
defaultSource.instrument: 8 CFR 212.1 (a visa is required of every arriving nonimmigrant except the listed classes: Canadian and Bermudian citizens, Bahamians pre-inspected in the Bahamas, citizens of the Marshall Islands and Micronesia, and Visa Waiver Program travellers under 8 CFR 217)

fee.notes: Payable online by card. Covers tourism, business and transit under the Visa Waiver Program; only for nationals of VWP countries.

source.name: ESTA — Official U.S. Customs and Border Protection application site
source.instrument: Travel Promotion Act of 2009 (Pub. L. 111-145), fee as updated by Pub. L. 119-21

fee.notes: Non-refundable application (MRV) fee. Requires the DS-160 form and, for most applicants, an in-person interview; appointment wait times vary widely by consulate and can reach several months.

source.name: 22 CFR 22.1 — Schedule of Fees for Consular Services
source.instrument: 22 CFR 22.1, Schedule of Fees for Consular Services, Item 21(a)

fee.notes: Plus the SEVIS I-901 fee of $350. Requires a Form I-20 from a SEVP-certified school; admitted for "duration of status" rather than a fixed number of days.

fee.notes: The US has no airside transit — every passenger clears immigration, so transiting travelers need a C-1 visa unless they hold ESTA or another valid visa. Validity and number of entries depend on the reciprocity schedule for your nationality.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay, unless your country is on the US six-month exemption list, in which case it only needs to be valid for the length of the stay. The list covers most of Europe, the UK, Canada, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, India and many others. It includes every Visa Waiver country except Brunei, but not China, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Kenya or Ghana, for example.

source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Six-Month Passport Validity Update (Carrier Liaison Program, 18 December 2025)

travelInsurance.text: No official source states a travel-insurance requirement for visitors to the United States. Medical treatment is expensive, and some hospitals ask non-residents for a deposit on admission, so comprehensive medical cover is essential.

source.name: USA.gov — Entering the United States

onwardTicket.text: Travelers entering under the Visa Waiver Program (ESTA) must hold a return or onward ticket; visitor visa holders may also be asked to show one.

source.name: ESTA — Official CBP application site

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is set. Visa Waiver travelers arriving at a land border must show evidence of financial solvency and a home abroad they will return to. Visa applicants may be asked at interview to show they can pay all the costs of the trip.

source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Visa Requirements and Visa Waiver Program conditions

currencyLimits.text: Currency and monetary instruments totalling more than $10,000 must be reported to CBP on arrival and departure (FinCEN Form 105). There is no limit on how much you may carry — only a reporting duty.

source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Know Before You Go: Money

notes: Visitors may generally bring 1 liter of alcohol and 200 cigarettes duty-free, plus gifts up to about $100 in value.
Agricultural rules are strict. Declare all food; fresh fruit, meat and plant products are usually prohibited.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted virtually everywhere, and a credit card is expected for hotels and car rental. Tipping is customary — 15–20% in restaurants. Displayed prices usually exclude sales tax.

safety.text: The UK FCDO advises against travel to no part of the US. It notes that violent and gun crime rarely affect tourists but asks visitors to take care in unfamiliar areas, that protests are common and can turn violent, and that medical treatment is expensive.

source.name: UK FCDO — USA travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring and early fall suit most regions; the country spans every climate from Alaska to Florida, so the ideal window depends on where you go.

idp.text: United States is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

driving.text: United States is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for United States yet.

tips.text: Apply for ESTA only at the official site esta.cbp.dhs.gov ($40.27) — third-party websites charge large mark-ups for the same application.
Submit your ESTA at least 72 hours before departure. Approval is usually quick but is not guaranteed, and airlines will deny boarding without it.
B1/B2 interview appointment wait times at some US consulates run to many months. Book your appointment long before planning travel dates.
A simple emergency-room visit can cost thousands of dollars — never travel to the US without medical insurance.

faq.question: What is ESTA and who needs it?
faq.answer: ESTA is the online travel authorization for the US Visa Waiver Program. Citizens of VWP countries (including the UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) must obtain it before boarding. It costs $40.27, is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the US with ESTA?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days per visit, for tourism, business or transit. The stay cannot be extended, and quick border runs to Canada or Mexico do not reset the 90-day clock.

faq.question: How much does a US visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The B1/B2 visitor visa application fee is $185. The visa is typically issued as a multiple-entry visa valid up to 10 years for many nationalities, and each admission allows a stay of up to 6 months.

faq.question: Do Canadian citizens need ESTA or a visa for the US?
faq.answer: No. Canadian citizens can enter the United States for tourism or business without a visa or ESTA and stay for up to 6 months.

faq.question: Is Romania in the US Visa Waiver Program?
faq.answer: No. Romania was designated for the Visa Waiver Program in January 2025, but the designation was rescinded on 2 May 2025 before it took effect, so Romanian citizens need a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185).
